column3: “to one another” renders “each to his brother.”
“an exceedingly good land” renders “the land is very, very good.”
“our prey” renders “our bread,” and “their protection” renders “their shade (tsel).”
“He promised them by oath” renders “he swore to them.”

“slow to anger” renders “long of nostrils,” and “abundant in lovingkindness” renders “great in hesed”; “will by no means clear the guilty” renders an emphatic doubled verb, with “the guilty” supplied.
“but indeed, as I live” renders the oath formula “but by my life.”
“shall by no means see” renders the oath formula “if they will see.”
“has followed Me fully” renders “has filled after me.”
“the valleys” renders the singular “the valley (emeq),” and “the Red Sea” renders “Sea of Reeds.”
NASB supplies “shall I bear with” in the question “How long … this evil congregation.”
“I swore” renders “I lifted up my hand,” and “Surely you shall not come” renders the oath formula “if you will come.”
